corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark with public harness and CPU stated, but the C++ compiler is not named, so it falls short of tier A. Server and wrk (4 threads) share the single vCPU, so the load generator competes with the server for CPU; one run, no variance reported. The numbers were recorded in the 2.1.0 release (CHANGELOG, 2026-03-19) and have not been re-measured on the current 2.5.0; the same 2.1.0 release also fixed a use-after-free in sendHeader() (the call the benchmark handler makes), and the page does not say whether the run came before or after that fix. docs/modules/http.md quotes the same numbers but gives a different load (wrk -t4 -c400 -d30s) than the perf README and CHANGELOG (-t4 -c100 -d10s). The handler returns an empty 200 with no routing, TLS or body, so this measures per-request framework overhead only. With Connection: close the claim disappears (Go 14,723 versus icey 14,330 req/s); the README headline table shows only the keep-alive rows. The Go server is default net/http (goroutine-per-connection, no tuning), and the README's statement that icey, Go and Node 'all share the same foundation (libuv ... llhttp)' is wrong for Go, which uses its own netpoller and parser. The project's headline claim (lightweight libwebrtc alternative, media stack) has no numeric comparison: the README table against libWebRTC, libdatachannel and GStreamer is qualitative (build time 'Hours' versus 'Minutes', binary size '50MB+' versus 'Small'), so this record documents the HTTP module only.

notes: Numbers on the perf README match the record exactly (keep-alive 72,209 vs Go 53,878 req/s, 34%; Connection: close 14,330 vs 14,723). Harness code is fair-looking (identical empty-200 handlers with Content-Length: 0 across icey, Go, Node). Shortcomings to record: compiler unstated, wrk on the same single vCPU, single run, numbers from 2.1.0 not re-run, inconsistent wrk parameters between docs and perf README, parity with Go under Connection: close, false 'same foundation' claim for Go, media-stack claims purely qualitative. Category http-servers-frameworks (wave 5 category, Go net/http baseline as for Drogon, Lwan, Crow) is outside wave 10's categories. Duplicate risk: seeds.json also lists https://github.com/sourcey/libsourcey (awesome-cpp frameworks), which is this same repo under its old name; fold it as duplicate if a seed pass picks it up.
